meaning.evidence: Every fact survives: dates, offices, Saturday hours, $10, the $2.50 fee, tag sizes (with helpful metric), the free permit for the school year, and the thinning rationale. "Year 4 kids" sensibly localises fourth graders.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "people who can't cut their own tree get first dibs", "just pop in the pass or voucher number", "heads up: the $2.50 service fee still applies", "does the bush a good turn".

authenticity.evidence: Natural, plain-spoken Australian; the one tic is the repeated "Chrissie tree", which Australians say but not eight times in a notice.

register.evidence: A light, friendly layer right for level 2: "first dibs", "heads up", "have a proper read"; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Keeps the informative, helpful tone of a public notice, just friendlier: "Get in touch with us for current opening hours."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Buy one online through recreation.gov and there's an extra $2.50 service fee on top."

variety.evidence: Varied apart from the leaned-on "Chrissie tree".
